subject: Dedicated GPU capacity briefing and pool-provisioning deep dive
messages:
From: Alexa Morales <alexa@finnova.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@finnova.com>
Date: 2027-05-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity review — FinNova POC

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the quick intro last week. FinNova is moving an evaluation forward for dedicated GPU capacity to support low-latency inference for a payments-risk product. Before our procurement push we need a technical deep-dive focused on: pool sizing, autoscaling behavior under burst traffic, and workload isolation/tenancy for regulated data.

High-level requirements:
- 2M tokens/day (spiky distribution, peak 4x baseline)
- P95 latency target < 120ms for single-request inference
- Isolation so that one business unit's workload cannot evict another

Can your team run a 60–90 minute architecture review next week? We prefer mornings PT. Also please share any prep worksheet or telemetry you want us to fill out ahead of the call.

Thanks,
Alexa Morales
Head of Platform
FinNova
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Alexa Morales <alexa@finnova.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-11T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity review — FinNova POC

Hi Alexa — great summary, thanks. We can do a technical deep-dive that covers exactly the items you listed. Proposed format (90 minutes):

Agenda:
- 10m: Introductions & current FinNova workload profile
- 20m: Pool sizing methodology & cost tradeoffs (steady vs burst capacity)
- 20m: Autoscaling policies, pre-warming, and cold-start behavior
- 15m: Isolation patterns (tenant isolation, network/KMS considerations)
- 15m: Failover, fallback model variants, and runbook/SLAs
- 10m: Next steps / procurement handoff

Proposed slots (PT):
- Thu May 13, 10:00–11:30am PT
- Fri May 14, 03:00–04:30pm PT

I've attached a short worksheet (FINNOVA_MATP_ROADMAP.pdf) that captures traffic shapes and data residency constraints — if you can drop numbers into the sheet it will speed the sizing discussion. Also linking a capacity worksheet for your infra team: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1a2b3c-capacity-worksheet

If either slot works tell me which one and I'll send a calendar invite with a short pre-read. Karthik will present sizing rationale; Marissa will cover procurement and contract/SLAs.

Cheers,
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Alexa Morales <alexa@finnova.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-11T12:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity review — FinNova POC

Adding Ben to the thread — he'll lead the ops portion and demo autoscale failover/runbook behavior. Ben, FYI we expect to walk through a sample pool config and a few stress scenarios. I'm attaching the config skeleton we'll reference (redwood_pool_config_v1.yaml).

Alexa — once we confirm a time I'll include Ben and our SRE dial-in so we can show a short live runbook demo (non-prod).

- Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
From: Alexa Morales <alexa@finnova.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@finnova.com>
Date: 2027-05-12T16:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity review — FinNova POC

Thanks everyone — we appreciate the quick turnaround and the agenda looks good. Unfortunately an exec stakeholder just pushed a conflicting board review into the May 13 window. Can we move the deep-dive to:

- Tue May 18, 09:00–10:30am PT

If that works for your team we'll confirm and add a calendar hold. Also requesting that you share the worksheet and the small YAML sample in editable form so our infra lead can annotate ahead of time.

Apologies for the churn — quoted below for context.
